key_design_notes: Gate order is the security contract: byte size + container sniff -> loadsStrict -> import string/asset bounds -> prototype audit -> closed-schema validate -> decoded-asset audit. Every stage rejects before the next stage's resource use exists.

PNG is dependency-free TypeScript: signature/chunk/CRC/IHDR checks, all color types and bit depths (0,2,3,4,6 x 1,2,4,8,16), Adam7, five filters, pixel cap 4 MP and edge cap 8192 enforced at IHDR before allocation, inflate capped at exact raster size, then re-encoded to a clean 8-bit RGBA PNG with no ancillary chunks/APNG. HTML/report consumers must use sanitizedPngs, never the imported bytes.
MIME/signature/hash: only image/png and application/pdf per contract; magic checked, sha256 and byte_length recomputed even though validate() already verified them (defense in depth).

assertScriptFreeHtml entity-decodes attribute values before checking so the exporter's own ' escaping and &#x…; smuggling cannot hide a scheme; dangerous tokens are checked inside markup attributes and <style> blocks only, so escaped report text may legitimately quote them.
fuzz_reports.py is stdlib-only and offline; the node driver arms egress tripwires and reports per-case ContractError codes; the run receipt carries a deterministic stream_sha256.
limitations: tsc typecheck not run: node_modules absent in this worktree; lockfiles frozen. Runtime coverage via node --test exercises every module.
Sanitized PNG output uses stored deflate — larger than compressed input but bounded by the 4 MP cap; correctness over compression ratio.
html_export_double.mjs is a test double of the reference exporter, not the T16 product exporter.
